messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing a cluster of Xid 79 + Xid 13 on gpunode-ukc-07 over the last 3 hours. Affected pods seem to be decode-heavy tenants (streaming chat). :eyes:

devin: I saw that alert too. infra-alertbot posted a couple of spikes: infra-alertbot: GPU gpunode-ukc-07:card2 Xid 79 (3 events), card3 Xid 13 (5 events) in 2h.

sam: Quick dump of `nvidia-smi` ECC counters from card2 (node gpunode-ukc-07):
```
$ nvidia-smi -i 2 -q -d Ecc
Product Name : A10G
ECC Errors (Volatile):
  Single Bit:  10237
  Double Bit:  2
  Retired Pages: 0
```
Not massive, but the timing lines up with the degraded decodes.

maya: Also grabbing dmesg around the timestamps, saw repeated lines: `NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus` followed by `NVRM: Xid (13): parent process killed` for some pids.

devin: Do we have workload metadata? Which models/quantizations? Could be correlated with long KV caching and many small token calls.

sam: Checked tenant telemetry: tenant "chatflow" is using llama-13b q4_0 with streaming, avg seq len ~640, concurrent sessions spiky at ~120 on that node.

kira: That's a lot of concurrent decode state per card. Could be persistent GPU memory pressure + thermal leading to Xid 79. Any thermal sensors?

sam: Temps acceptable: 66C average on card2, but power draw spikes to 285W during bursts and node-level PSU reports 3 transient undervolt events in last 6h.

devin: Hypothesis: sustained high-power bursts + occasional power transient => bus/drop => Xid 79. Xid 13 might be cleanup from oom/driver aborts during those drops.

ops-lead: Proposal: 1) Immediately cordon gpunode-ukc-07 and migrate hot tenants off (canary drain). 2) Run targeted stress test to reproduce. 3) If Xid rate > 3/hour after stress, schedule hardware replace.

maya: I'll kick off the cordon+drain now for low-impact window. Devin, can you run a reproduce test with a copy of chatflow on a lab node? Use same model config and concurrency.

devin: On it. Will run the exact client workload from `infra/playbooks/chatflow-replay.sh` and log `dmesg -w` + `nvidia-smi -l 5` for 1 hour.

kira: Also please capture the kernel driver version + CUDA runtime: `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` + `nvcc --version` on the node, and attach. We had a driver micro-regression last month that raised Xid 31 under edge cases.

sam: For the replacement threshold, I suggest we use a pragmatic rule: >10 Xid 79 events in 24h OR >5 Xid 13 events in 6h for the same GPU => mark RETIRE. Otherwise escalate to on-site diagnostics (PSU, riser).

maya: Noted. I'll update the node ticket with that threshold. Ticket: INFRA-4237.

infra-alertbot: alert created INFRA-4237: gpunode-ukc-07 cards flagged for Xid anomalies.

ops-lead: Action items: Maya (drain + update ticket), Devin (repro + logs), Sam (compile ECC/trend report for last 30 days), Kira (coordinate on-site stack check if retire triggered). We'll reconvene in #eng-sre in 2h unless reproducer fires earlier. :thumbsup:

maya: Done — cordon applied, starting gradual drain. Will post progress updates in this thread.

devin: Reproducer started. Posting logs to the ticket link in 30m.

sam: I'll start the ECC aggregation job now and post a CSV to the ticket.

kira: Thx. If we confirm power transients, plan is to swap riser and test. If issue persists, RMA card.

maya: Update: two pods migrated off, drained 40% of sessions, no new Xids in the last 12m. Keeping cordon until reproduction completes.

devin: Reproducer hit a burst and I captured one Xid 79 on lab-gpu-04 within 18m, matching the decode pattern. Attaching minimal logs in ticket.

ops-lead: Good repro. Next steps: schedule 1h on-site for PSU/riser on gpunode-ukc-07 tomorrow morning. Sam proceed with retire if on-site finds riser faulty.

maya: Closing loop here — will leave node out of rotation until hardware check. Thanks team.
